examples.text: He was by birth, some authors write, / A Russian, some a Muscovite, / And 'mong the Cossacks had been bred, / Of whom we in diurnals read.

trans.sense: excessive production of urine — see also polyuria

raw_glosses: (biology, medicine) Excessive production of urine; polyuria.
(biology, medicine) (more often) The physiologic process that produces such an increase.
glosses: (more often) The physiologic process that produces such an increase.

raw_glosses: (biology, medicine) (most often) The administration of medications to encourage that process.
glosses: (most often) The administration of medications to encourage that process.

examples.text: Blackcurrant leaf has a diuretic action [11,12,14], therefore it should not be taken concurrently with diuretics indicated for cardiac or renal insufficiency except on medical advice.
examples.ref: 2003, European Scientific Cooperative on Phytotherapy, ESCOP Monographs: The Scientific Foundation for Herbal Medicinal Products, page 426:

examples.text: Since vasodilatation is a side effect of diuretics but also occurs in thermoregulation, diuretics should be reduced in meteoropathic individuals to prevent extremely dangerous situations [38, 39].
examples.ref: 2023 June 15, Malvina Hoxha, Bruno Zappacosta, “Meteoropathy: a review on the current state of knowledge”, in Journal of Medicine and Life, volume 16, number 6, →DOI, archived from the original on 14 Jul 2025, pages 837-841:

raw_glosses: (medicine, pharmacology) A drug or a substance that increases the rate of urine excretion.
glosses: A drug or a substance that increases the rate of urine excretion.
